title: Natural Q&A #6
summary: NH answers viewer questions on where his knowledge comes from, leaving France, marriage, avoiding burnout, training in a freezing garage, training time of day, collaborations, video games, never getting sick, nature vs nurture, debating fitness YouTubers, fixing 'bad' lats, learning English, recomposition timelines, anime and his empty-mind state while lifting. Fitness content is mixed with lots of life philosophy.
claims: Most of what NH teaches comes from personal experimentation in and out of the gym, tested enough times to believe it carries over; he avoids topics where he isn't solid
Paying attention to what happens in your own training sessions teaches more relevant programming knowledge than books
Musashi's idea 'from one thing, ten thousand things': once you discover one nugget of knowledge, it becomes easy to keep digging
NH left France because of its government and institutions; he felt there was no future for someone like him there
He prefers North America's emphasis on liberty over Europe's safety nets, which he thinks make people stop trying
He earns about twice as much in North America as he would in France for the same job
NH is a fierce defender of marriage: a union is functionally stronger and more resource-efficient than a solitary life
Don't marry too young, e.g. at 18; give yourself and the other person time to grow up
Teenagers should focus on developing themselves rather than dating; to find the one you need to be the one
Marriage is sacred; its destruction came from attempts to desacralize it
The brain has no max capacity; NH deliberately overloads himself and finds himself twice as productive two weeks later
Be at peace with your current knowledge, expand from it, specialize in what attracts you but leave your comfort zone sometimes
Beginner burnout is usually over-stimulation, not overtraining: doing two-hour workouts you aren't prepared for
Beginners should start with about 25-minute sessions three times a week and ramp up gradually
The person who trains properly for 10 years outgrows the one who trains very intensely for six months then quits
There are three levels: motivation, discipline, and just doing it; long-time naturals train because it's on the schedule, without deliberation
NH's garage gym is near outdoor temperature: about 90°F in summer, usually 30°F in winter, sometimes 15-20°F
Training in extreme cold, his feet went numb at first, but his body adapted so that he became fine at 25°F
Training in a freezer-like garage after a nine-hour shift builds mental toughness: if you can train there you can train anywhere
NH trains daily from about 4:30-8:00 or 5:30-8:30 pm after work, resting on Sundays
He is not a morning person; he is strongest around 5-8 pm, but people can adapt to training at any time; learn your internal clock
NH avoids collabs because he dislikes socializing, his anti-supplement stance makes him enemies in YouTube fitness, and he likes the channel self-contained
He warms up clothed and strips as he goes to force his body to produce heat; he finds his muscles stay warm until the end of the workout
NH quit video games around 21 because they are a time sink for addictive personalities; League of Legends made him depressed
He hasn't had a cold or flu in about 10 years since he started training daily at 15
He attributes his immunity to good nutrition without processed food, lots of water, enough sleep and not hiding from the cold
NH avoids medication like painkillers for headaches or cough remedies, letting his body handle it
Raw garlic can boost the immune system
When he feels like he might be getting sick, training makes the feeling go away; training is the best thing for immunity
Personality has a genetic base via brain chemistry, but environment can strongly reshape it
Online debates are pointless because people delete arguments, argue dishonestly, or big YouTubers suppress footage to protect their brands
NH thought he had terrible lat insertions (and calves) because he relied on deadlifts; he had a 500 lb deadlift and nonexistent lats
His lats grew once he did strict pull-ups and pullovers every day
Rows and deadlifts are often done with the legs and lower back; lats need strict movements such as pull-ups, Australian pull-ups and pullovers
Recommends Frédéric Delavier's biomechanics work and French channel
Language learning: watch a show with native subtitles, then target-language subtitles, then none; read a known book in the language; speak; then immerse
Doing a learning ritual right before bed helps retention and consistency
Body fat misestimates of 5% on a 200+ lb advanced lifter represent many pounds of supposed lean mass that isn't there
For someone NH's size, recomping 2% body fat is about 4-5 lb of fat into muscle and takes years (3-7)
Losing a few percent body fat is faster with a cut or aggressive deficit (which he doesn't recommend), and easier for lighter people
Never let anyone, including NH, discourage you
NH has read manga and watched anime since age 10, back when it made you an outcast
Mocking anime fans reflects conformism and lack of empathy; dismissing all anime is like dismissing all cinema
If kept up very late, sleep instead of training; forced workouts without energy have given him bad sessions or injuries
Learn to say no to social pressure that would wreck your sleep and next-day training
NH loves Attack on Titan, read it since its French release, and thinks its political message is simple yet misunderstood
NH can turn off inner chatter; while lifting he thinks of nothing but the body moving, and he carried that mind state outside the gym
exercises: lats; deadlifts alone did not grow them
